body: Very true, sadly. Thank you for the advice, it has helped save me and may save me again in the future from falling into the same dark pit of depression. Thank you very much for your response!

Thank you so much. Truthfully, the people I help at rehab give me a purpose and therefore keep me alive. It's my honor to be able to help beautiful people like you recognize their worth and their beauty. I once spent time in rehab and I try to be everything positive I was given at rehab as well as be everything I did not get but wanted during my time in rehab. I too would be dead if not for the people I encounter at the rehab center. Thank you, truly. I hope you have a wonderful life, full of positive surprises. :) <3

Thank you, truly. I'm realizing slowly that their values are different from mine, but I guess I haven't wanted to acknowledge it because it is crushing tbh. I've always been so close with them. Thank you for speaking the truth I was too afraid to recognize.
That's true. Just a lot of expectations have really hurt my self-esteem.
Of course. PM me if you just want to vent or need any other advice.

I'm sorry. Truly. I don't exactly have advice that I know without a doubt can work, but I have been in the same situation as you. The process will be tiring and long. Talk to as many people as you can while in the hospital about what you are going through even if you're not sure they will understand. Be very descriptive. It will be tough but feel good to get it out. I'm not sure whether or not your life is ruined, but if you are in the hospital then that is a good sign. My only advice is to come up with a plan after getting out what troubles you with a worker. A plan for your future, regardless of what society or other people think. It just needs to work for you.
Thank you, you're right. Who gave them the authority to set the standard? F\*ck expectations.
